analysis.title: US Midterms / Dovish RBA / ECB Presidency / US-Iran Talks / Trump-Putin-Xi Meeting / US CPI
key_insights: US midterms are on Tuesday. UBS Evidence Lab puts the implied probability of Democratic House control at 97% (Republicans 7%) and of Democratic Senate control at 81% (Republicans 25%). The probabilities as printed sum to more than 100%.

UBS rates strategist Phoebe White says a Democratic sweep would only modestly flatten the US curve, and the move would likely be short-lived given narrow margins and gridlock. A Republican sweep could cause a significant long-end sell-off.

Phoebe White names three channels for rates risk: pressure on AI data centers to pay for electricity and grid costs, wider deficits next year if a split Congress does not restrain spending, and a Democratic Senate constraining Fed appointments and keeping the central bank more independent and less dovish.

Midterm pricing implies the largest one-day S&P 500 breakeven move through year-end at just over 1%. Focaldata's James Kanagasooriam says the double-digit Democratic generic polling lead looks overstated and sees the Senate as effectively a toss-up.

The RBA hiked 25bp to 4.85% with a 6-3 vote and dropped its tightening bias. UBS Economics reads this as clearly dovish and keeps its call for a hold. AUD traded softer and December RBA pricing eased to about 2.5bp from about 6bp. NZ election risk on Nov. 7 remains in play.

Eurogroup president Pierrakakis wants ECB president nominations by close of business Friday to replace Lagarde, who steps down Feb. 7. The shortlist is discussed Nov. 9. Known candidates are Hernandez de Cos and Knot, and Nagel and Moulin are reportedly considering it.

Oil is edging lower on the prospect of new US-Iran talks, with Brent down 6% this week, even though the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says it cannot consider reopening the Strait until all US sanctions are lifted and says Vance's offers are unchanged.
The FT reports a possible Trump, Putin and Xi meeting at APEC in about two weeks, possibly in Shenzhen. An agreed agenda is the obstacle, and either format would favour Xi as the lead figure.

UBS economist Alan Detmeister projects October headline CPI at +0.28% m/m, near consensus and down from September's 0.39%, with gasoline contributing 0.04pp versus 0.39pp. Core is projected at 0.23%, led by a 1.5% drop in used car prices. He sees no clear risk skew, relief for headline CPI only by next spring, and core CPI peaking early in 2027.

12-month CPI will not be published because of missing data from last year's government shutdown. PCE rates remain available and core PCE is expected to rise to 3.2%. UBS has 25bp Fed hikes priced for the December and January meetings.

World Gold Council data show central banks and official institutions bought a net 321 tonnes of gold in Q3, up 42% y/y and the most since Q4 2024. Physically backed gold ETFs took in 211 tonnes. Global bar-and-coin demand fell 19% y/y but China's rose 7%.

Treasury borrowing plans are close to Phoebe White's forecasts ($618bn for Oct-Dec 2026 versus her $635bn, $800bn for Jan-Mar 2027 versus her $771bn). She still expects no change in coupon auction sizes, with changes possible later in 2027.
Swiss October CPI rose to 1.5% y/y versus the 1.3% consensus, but UBS expects the SNB to hold at 0% on Dec. 10. December pricing is near 2bp and 15bp of hikes are priced for March.
Apple shares fell 0.24% against 3.9% implied volatility after a Q4 beat, with iPhone and Mac strength offset by softer iPad and Wearables. China sales were soft and guidance is the focus.

UBS Volatility Weekly says October saw the largest cross-asset correlation shift since the start of the Iran war. Bonds moved from selling off with risk to rallying when risk sells off. SPX/Rates and SPX/Yen implied correlations have not yet repriced, which the desk sees as an opportunity to add SPX risk-off hybrid hedges.

European energy delivered a 7% net income beat with every company beating for a second straight quarter, even after estimates were revised up 15% in the prior month. Downstream drove most of it. Analyst Joshua Stone found Eni and BP the most positive updates and Galp the weakest.

European equities are weak on AI selling and midterm caution. Oracle raised a further $20bn of capital. The Euro Stoxx 50 is down 1% and has fallen 3.3% since October while the STOXX Europe 600 has risen 1%, the pair's largest divergence drawdown in two years.

FX desk: EURUSD met supply above 1.1220 with French fiscal concerns still in place. For the BoE Thursday, a 25bp hike is expected and anything tighter than a 7-2 vote risks being read as a dovish hike. The desk prefers EURGBP over GBPUSD to express GBP strength.

market_movers.rationale: UBS analyst Joshua Stone named Eni one of the two most positive updates in a European energy quarter where every company beat consensus.
Named by Stone as one of the most positive updates in a quarter with a 7% sector net income beat, led by downstream.
Galp (no US listing) was the weakest update of the quarter after announcing no deal with Moeve.

sector_views.rationale: Net income beat consensus by 7% with every company beating for a second consecutive quarter, driven mostly by downstream. Stance inferred from Buy ratings on Eni, BP and Galp.

earnings_insights: Apple Q4 (reported): revenue $114.48bn versus $113.4bn expected, EPS $2.10 versus $1.99 expected. The report does not state whether EPS is GAAP or adjusted. Shares fell 0.24% versus 3.9% implied.

Apple Q1 expectations (consensus, not yet reported): revenue $152.2bn and EPS $2.90. No Q1 figures were given in the initial color, so guidance, China trends and launch-cycle commentary are the focus.

European energy delivered a 7% net income beat versus consensus in the latest reporting quarter, the second consecutive quarter in which every company beat. Estimates were revised up 15% in the month before results.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Dropping the tightening bias and the split vote read as dovish. UBS expects the RBA to hold from here.
A cooler gasoline contribution slows headline inflation from September's pace.
Led by a 1.5% drop in used car prices, with rent and hotel growth slowing.
PCE is expected to tick up while 12-month CPI is not published because of missing shutdown-related data.
Hot versus consensus but inside the SNB's 0-2% band, so UBS expects a December hold.
Falling farm prices offset petroleum up 14.9%. Fuel price caps cut headline inflation by an estimated 0.8pp.
Close to UBS forecasts, so no change in coupon auction sizes is expected near term.
Largest quarterly addition since Q4 2024, attributed to diversification and risk management.
The MPC vote split is the focus, with a split tighter than 7-2 risking a dovish read.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hikes priced for December and January FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: A December hike is UBS's base case, with a more patient 2027 path.

A split Congress may not restrain spending, widening deficits next year.
Renewed AI-related selling and funding concerns, including Oracle's further $20bn capital raise.
US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz with talks and strikes happening at once, and oil price swings.
BoE vote split tighter than 7-2 may read as a dovish hike, and a hawkish BoE shock could hit December gilt-linked contracts.
NZ election on Nov. 7 and French fiscal concerns.
Long-end supply and fiscal concerns around the QRA and elections.
vol_and_positioning: Midterm pricing implies the largest one-day S&P 500 breakeven move through year-end at just over 1%.
Apple fell 0.24% against 3.9% implied volatility after earnings.
Cross-asset correlations fell to their lowest in years. SPX/Rates and SPX/Yen implied correlations have not repriced, so UBS sees value in adding classic SPX risk-off hybrid hedges.
Desk flows are muted and positioning looks relatively light ahead of the midterms (FX desk, RBA note).
EURUSD move on Monday looked largely position-driven, helped by the oil correction and pre-election positioning.
geopolitical: US struck Iranian facilities on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran was launching surface-to-air missiles from it, while Trump and Vance tout new talks.

Iran says it cannot consider reopening the Strait of Hormuz until all US sanctions are lifted and is not ready to discuss its nuclear program. Pezeshkian was reportedly given authority by Khamenei to pursue talks.
FT reports officials are working on a possible Trump, Putin and Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen in about two weeks.
ECB presidency succession: nominations due Friday, Eurogroup discusses the shortlist Nov. 9.
NZ election on Nov. 7 with tight polling and coalition uncertainty.
Underlying fiscal concerns around France weigh on the euro.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic sweep would only modestly flatten the curve and the move would be short-lived given narrow margins and gridlock.
tension_points.bear_case: A Republican sweep could cause a significant long-end sell-off through AI data center cost pressure and wider deficits. Even a split Congress may not restrain spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Election results showing a Republican sweep would break the benign modest-flattening scenario. Focaldata sees the Senate as a toss-up, so early key-race results are the signal.

tension_points.bull_case: A 25bp hike is widely expected, with the market pricing around 100bp more by Sep'27, supporting GBP.
tension_points.bear_case: An MPC vote tighter than 7-2 risks being read as a dovish hike, and a hawkish shock could sell off December contracts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A vote split tighter than 7-2 on Thursday would undermine the GBP-strength reading.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil is falling on the potential for new talks, as Iran's president was reportedly authorized to pursue them.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran's conditions are unchanged (all sanctions lifted before reopening the Strait) and the US struck Qeshm Island hours after the conciliatory comments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Iran agreeing to talks without all US sanctions lifted would change the standoff. The report says it is unclear whether anything has changed.
